Russia's Fort Ross in northern California was established in 1812 and sold in 1841. U.S. forces took the northern ports in 1846, Californios surrendered in the Treaty of Cahuenga on January 13, 1847, and Mexico ceded California in 1848.

eras.polity: United States — ceded California, not yet a state
eras.note: The Gold Rush began in 1848. California was admitted as a state on September 9, 1850 with no territorial period.
Statewide registration of births and deaths began in 1905. Earlier events are in the county recorder's records, and some counties kept records from the mid-1800s.

regions.label: Nevada — Great Basin to the Comstock
regions.sub: Reno, Carson City, Virginia City, Las Vegas, Elko

eras.polity: Claimed as part of Spanish Alta California
eras.note: Before registers. Present-day Nevada lay within the territory of Alta California; the Franciscan Francisco Garcés was the first European to enter the area, in the 1770s.
Mexican Alta California included present-day Nevada. Jedediah Smith entered the Las Vegas Valley in 1827.
Utah Territory, organised on September 9, 1850, covered most of present-day Nevada. Mormon way stations from 1851 began a permanent American presence, and the Comstock Lode was discovered in 1859.
Congress created Nevada Territory on March 2, 1861.

Nevada was admitted on October 31, 1864; its eastern and southern boundaries were enlarged in 1866-67, so places in the east and south were earlier in other territories. The state holds birth and death records from July 1, 1911, and earlier records are generally with the county recorder.

regions.label: Utah — Mexican ground to Deseret and Utah Territory
regions.sub: Salt Lake City, Ogden, Provo, St. George, Logan

eras.polity: Claimed as part of Spanish Alta California
eras.note: Before registers. The Spanish province of Alta California was described as including all of present-day Utah.
Utah lay within Mexican Alta California until the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo of 1848. The Mormon pioneers entered the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847, when the land still belonged to Mexico.

eras.polity: State of Deseret (provisional) in ceded territory
eras.note: The Mormon settlers formed the provisional State of Deseret, dated to March 12, 1849 in one study; it served as the de facto government before Congress acted. Sources differ on when Deseret ended (1850 or 1851).

Congress organised Utah Territory on September 9, 1850; it then covered present Utah, most of Nevada, western Colorado and a corner of Wyoming, and lost ground when Nevada Territory and Colorado Territory were formed in 1861 and Wyoming Territory in 1868. Fillmore was the capital to 1856, then Salt Lake City. A Church History Library database names the pioneers who came to Utah from 1847 to 1868.

Utah became the 45th state on January 4, 1896. Statewide birth and death registration began in 1905, with county clerks keeping registers from 1898; the Utah State Archives holds the permanent records.

regions.label: Colorado — from Kansas, Nebraska, Utah and New Mexico territories
regions.sub: Denver, Pueblo, Colorado Springs, Durango, San Luis

eras.polity: Spanish claim south and west of the Arkansas River
eras.note: Before registers. Juan Bautista de Anza founded San Carlos near present-day Pueblo in 1787, and the settlement quickly failed.
The Treaty of Córdoba gave Mexico Spain's territorial claims in 1821. The Arkansas River line was set by the Adams-Onís Treaty of 1819: U.S. claims south and west of the river were ceded to Spain.

eras.polity: Kansas, Nebraska, Utah and New Mexico territories
eras.note: Before February 28, 1861 a Colorado place lay in Kansas, Nebraska, Utah or New Mexico territory, so earlier county and probate records are filed under those. The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) opened the southern Rockies to American settlement, the Pikes Peak Gold Rush began in July 1858, and the extralegal Jefferson Territory existed from October 24, 1859 to 1861. In the Compromise of 1850 Texas gave up claims to land including parts of present-day Colorado.

Congress organised Colorado Territory on February 28, 1861 and the legislature created 17 counties on November 1, 1861. The Sand Creek Massacre took place in November 1864 during the Colorado War of 1863-65.
Colorado became the 38th state on August 1, 1876. Statewide birth and death registration began in 1907, though some counties began as early as 1876; the Colorado State Archives is in Denver.

regions.label: Montana and Wyoming — Louisiana Purchase and Oregon Country to territories
regions.sub: Billings, Helena, Missoula, Cheyenne, Casper, Laramie

eras.polity: Louisiana Purchase east of the Continental Divide; Oregon Country west of it
eras.note: Wyoming's ground east of the Continental Divide and Montana's east of it were part of the 1803 Louisiana Purchase; ground west of the Divide and north of the 42nd parallel was in the Oregon Country, where Britain and the United States shared access from 1818 until the Oregon Treaty of June 15, 1846. A corner of southwestern Wyoming came to the U.S. in the Mexican Cession of 1848.

eras.polity: Oregon, Washington, Nebraska, Dakota and Utah territories
eras.note: Ground west of the Divide lay in Oregon Territory (1848), then Washington Territory (1853); ground east of it lay in Nebraska Territory and from March 2, 1861 in Dakota Territory, which then included much of present Montana and Wyoming. Records before 1863 therefore sit under those territories.

eras.polity: Idaho Territory, Montana Territory and Dakota Territory
eras.note: Idaho Territory was created on March 3 or 4, 1863 (dated differently by source) out of land that included Dakota's. Montana Territory was organised from Idaho Territory on May 26, 1864 (dated May 28 in one account), and Wyoming Territory followed on July 25, 1868, formed from Dakota, Idaho and Utah territories.

Wyoming's territorial government was organised on April 17, 1869, and in 1872 the territory had five counties: Albany, Carbon, Laramie, Sweetwater and Uinta. Montana became a state on November 8, 1889, and Wyoming on July 10, 1890.

Statewide birth and death registration began in Montana in 1907 (practitioners were first required to keep records in 1895) and in Wyoming in 1909, with some earlier county registers in Albany and Laramie counties.

regions.label: Oregon — Oregon Country, Provisional Government, Territory and State
regions.sub: Portland, Salem, Eugene, Oregon City, Astoria, Pendleton, Medford

eras.polity: Oregon Country — joint British and American occupation
eras.note: An 1818 arrangement gave Britain and the United States shared access to the region. The Hudson's Bay Company had almost complete control after its 1821 merger with the North West Company and made Fort Vancouver its headquarters from 1825.

eras.polity: Oregon Country — joint occupation, settlers' Provisional Government
eras.note: The Provisional Government of Oregon ran from 1843 to 1849, during the last years of joint occupation.

eras.polity: Oregon Treaty — Provisional Government of Oregon
eras.note: The Oregon Treaty of June 15, 1846 settled the boundary with Britain, with the Oregon Country divided along the 49th parallel. The Provisional Government continued until 1849.

Congress created Oregon Territory in 1848 (14 August 1848; some sources give 1846). It covered present Idaho, Oregon and Washington and the parts of Montana and Wyoming west of the Continental Divide until Washington Territory was split off on March 2, 1853. The Donation Land Claim Act dates from 1850.

Oregon was admitted as a state on February 14, 1859 within its present boundaries. Statewide birth and death registration began under a 1903 law, though some counties began registering as early as 1845.

regions.label: Washington and Idaho — Oregon Country to territories and statehood
regions.sub: Seattle, Olympia, Spokane, Walla Walla, Vancouver WA, Boise, Lewiston

eras.polity: Oregon Country — joint British and American occupation
eras.note: An 1818 arrangement gave Britain and the United States shared access to the region. The Hudson's Bay Company had almost complete control after its 1821 merger with the North West Company and made Fort Vancouver its headquarters from 1825.

eras.polity: Oregon Treaty — Provisional Government of Oregon
eras.note: The Oregon Treaty of June 15, 1846 settled the boundary with Britain, with the Oregon Country divided along the 49th parallel. The Provisional Government of Oregon continued until 1849.

Congress created Oregon Territory in 1848 (14 August 1848; some sources give 1846). It covered present Idaho, Oregon and Washington and the parts of Montana and Wyoming west of the Continental Divide.
Washington Territory was created on March 2, 1853 and at its largest included all of present Idaho.
Idaho Territory was created on March 3 or 4, 1863 (dated differently by source), which gave Washington Territory its present boundaries.

eras.polity: United States — State of Washington and State of Idaho
eras.note: Washington became a state on November 11, 1889; Idaho followed on July 3, 1890, so Idaho records of 1889-90 are still territorial. Statewide death registration began in Washington in 1907 and in Idaho in 1911 (county-level registration is sometimes dated 1907 for Idaho).

regions.label: Alaska — Russian America to statehood
regions.sub: Sitka, Juneau, Kodiak, Anchorage, Fairbanks, Nome, the Aleutians

eras.note: Russia's first permanent Alaskan settlement was founded at Three Saints Bay, Kodiak, in 1784; the Russian-American Company was chartered in 1799 and New Archangel (Sitka) became the capital in 1808. The Russian Orthodox Church kept the parish registers: the Diocese of Alaska archives were deposited in the Library of Congress (by 1927 or 1940 depending on the source), with microfilm at the National Archives Pacific Alaska Region and the Alaska State Library, and FamilySearch has Alaska Russian Orthodox records for 1845-1917.
The United States bought Alaska in 1867 for $7.2 million and the formal transfer is dated October 18, 1867. Control passed among the Army, Treasury and Navy before civil administration began.
Alaska was reorganised as the District of Alaska in 1884. Gold in Canada's Yukon in 1896 and at Nome in 1899 brought gold-rush traffic through the district.

The Second Organic Act of 1912 made it the Territory of Alaska. In the Aleutian campaign of 1942-43 Japanese forces occupied Attu and Kiska; Aleut residents were evacuated or interned and the Attuans were resettled at Atka after the war.
Alaska was admitted as a state on January 3, 1959.

regions.label: Hawaii — Kingdom, Republic, Territory and State
regions.sub: Honolulu, Hilo, Lahaina, Kauai, Maui, Molokai

eras.note: Kamehameha I established the kingdom in 1795 and Kauai and Niihau joined in 1810, so the unification is dated 1795 or 1810 depending on the source. The monarchy was absolute until the constitution of 1840.

The Great Mahele of 1848 divided the land; each claim was either awarded a Land Commission Award or not, and the awards often name parents, siblings and spouses. The Hawaii State Archives holds marriage records from 1826 and birth and death records from 1853, which are incomplete before 1896.

eras.polity: Overthrow of the monarchy and the Republic of Hawaii
eras.note: The monarchy was overthrown on January 17, 1893 by the Committee of Safety, backed by U.S. forces. The Republic of Hawaii was established in 1894 and lasted until 1898.

The Newlands Resolution was signed on July 7, 1898 and annexation took effect on August 12, 1898. The Hawaiian Organic Act of April 30, 1900 organised the Territory, and martial law was in force from 1941 to 1944.
Hawaii was admitted as the 50th state on August 21, 1959.

regimeNote: Five of these carry a Wikidata id and the dates Wikidata holds for them. The rest do not, and that is deliberate: fuzzy matching offered Circassia for Croatia, Audhali for Australia and Basutoland for Poland, and several of the labels here — «Aquileia · Gorizia · Frankopan», «German occupation» — are this project's own shorthand for a situation rather than the name of a state. An honest blank beats a plausible lie. data/polities-wikidata.json holds 1,857 former countries with dates as a REFERENCE for whoever authors the next region, not as something a machine should match automatically.
regimeArchivesNote: `archives` is WHICH MODERN STATE HELD THIS GROUND under that regime — the country whose flag flew over it, and whose archive inherited the paper. Habsburg is AT and HU because the Dual Monarchy filed in both capitals; Galicia is PL and UA because the border of 1945 cut it and its archives in half. It is NOT a claim about who owns the ground today, and it is not a border: it is the answer to «whose archive do I write to for these years, and whose flag was over the parish when the entry was made». A regime that left no single successor state — the Aquileia/Gorizia/Frankopan feudal centuries — carries an empty list on purpose, because a guess at which modern capital inherited a patriarchate is exactly the inference this atlas refuses elsewhere. Read by abroadFor() for the «also governed from» sources, and by eraFlagsHtml() for the flags over the selected era.
countriesNote: Derived from each ring — the vertices, the edge midpoints and the centre — rather than from the places walked inside it. A region is a piece of ground and which countries it covers is a fact about the ground, not about whether anybody has walked a parish in it yet. A country claimed by a single sampled point is dropped as a corner clipping a neighbour.
